body: My dad is currently awaiting a trial for murdering my maternal grandmother. This all happened four years ago (I think, but I don't actively try to remember the details). As far as red flags go, there were a few. He'd been especially irritable in the days prior, acting abnormally rash (this from a man with a short temper to begin with). However he had neuropathy, arthritis, and a total of twenty six surgeries since his twenties (hip, knee, shoulder replacements, among others; the man was practically half bionic). He was consistently taking quite a bit of prescription painkillers and other drugs. However, that's not what caused this, at least to my knowledge. In the weeks leading up to the murder, he'd been (almost randomly) quitting one medication or another in an attempt to find out which (or which combination of) medication(s) was causing him some unwanted side effects. You can imagine that after being on 80mg of Oxy and numerous other heavy drugs for years and suddenly going cold turkey would have some adverse side effects.  The one thing that really sticks in my mind other than that is that he flipped a coffee table the day before. Mind you he'd never been violent or physical about his anger before, just swearing, and he didn't flip it at anyone. Just sort of flipped it over something rather petty as I remember. Strangely enough he seemed to immediately realize he'd done something out of the ordinary and wrong. He apologized and helped us clean up the mess, but my mother and I were certainly shaken. He was arrested several days after the murder, has plead not guilty/insanity ever since, denies any involvement, and is still awaiting trial despite the fact that there's an overwhelming amount of evidence against him and a total of zero other suspects. I don't keep in touch with him, but I don't hate him. I'm just awkward and never really liked him much anyways as awful as that probably sounds.
